notes:
# 0.15.158

**Settings can no longer freeze the app, screen sharing is sharper, and a share you open fills the
call.**

## Settings froze the whole app

Derek's recording: Settings → My profile, press ×, *"Discard profile changes?"* with nothing edited;
press Discard, and the question vanished but its dim stayed — Settings open behind it, nothing taking
a click until Blackline was restarted. Every ×, every time.

Two faults, both fixed:

- **A question about edits nobody made.** A profile saved when the banner could have its own colour is
  shown in today's one-colour form, with Save offered so what you see is what everyone gets. That
  same flag was read as "you have unsaved edits". There are two flags now: Save can be on, but only
  your own changes are ever asked about.
- **A question hidden by the one before it.** Discard closed the first question and, from inside that,
  asked again; the first one's fade-out then hid the second while its dim stayed. A closing question
  can no longer hide one opened after it — anywhere in the app, not only here.

`test/e2e-settings-close.mjs` walks it with exactly that kind of profile. Against the old code it
reproduces the freeze; against this one it passes.

## Sharper screen sharing

Measured before changing anything (`test/audit/share-quality.mjs`, a 1080p text pattern, clean, at
100 ms, and at 100 ms with 1% loss): **every blurry moment was the picture being made smaller.** At
full size, text held up even at 100 ms with loss; at 720p one-pixel detail was gone, at 540p erased —
and the share spent over half of a clean minute below 1080p, because it was told to protect its frame
rate before its detail. So:

- **A share keeps its resolution** under pressure and gives up frame rate instead. A slower frame of
  text is still readable; a smaller one is not.
- **It is treated as detail, not motion.**
- **It starts at 6 Mb/s** instead of the engine's ~300 kb/s guess, which took 10–20 s to climb to full
  size every time.
- **The desktop's capture step is near-lossless now.** Each frame passes through a JPEG on its way to
  the call; at quality 75 (with colour halved) text came out at 36.5 dB and coloured text at 26.4 dB
  before the call's encoder even saw it. At 90, with full colour, it is 44.6 and 37.0. It costs more
  per frame, so a share asked for more than 30 fps gets a fourth encoder to keep its pace.

Lip sync was measured too — the sound arrives 70–110 ms before the picture — and is **not** fixed in
this release; it is next.

## A share you open fills the call

Click a shared screen and it now takes **the whole conversation** — the call grows from its strip to
fill it, the chat moves to the side — instead of being enlarged inside a 340-pixel strip. Under a wide
picture the other people sit in a small row below it, above the call's buttons; beside a tall one they
sit at the side. Click it again, or let the share end, and everything goes back.

## Smaller things

- **Notifications** show Blackline's mark as a small square beside the words, not a picture across the
  whole notification.
- **A message is announced once.** The same message arriving twice (a second route, a redelivery) no
  longer raises a second notification or counts as unread twice.
- **In a call with someone, their conversation's call buttons step aside** — there is nothing to start.
- **"Ask to be given it" is now "Request control"**, and the permission is called *Request remote
  control*.
- **The details pane** no longer runs a label under its value when the value is long
  ("Reachable on …").

## Still open

- Lip sync (sound ahead of the picture by 70–110 ms).
- The call view is being redesigned from a written spec: two-person calls simple, stacking only for
  meetings, checked at every window size including the popped-out one.
- Noise suppression is the browser's basic one; an AI suppressor like Discord's is planned, measured
  first.
- A space still does not reach a second device of the same account; `e2e-calls` step 16 is red, as it
  was.
